title: Compute ray march: directional light, basic self-shadowing, HDR output
summary: Add a compute ray marcher that samples the 3D density, applies Beer-Lambert absorption and a single directional light with in-volume shadowing, and writes to HDR.
motivation: First visual of the real volumetric effect; enables iterating lighting and quality controls.
scope: Shader: raymarch.hlsl (cs_6_0) → RWTexture2D<float4> HDR, Texture3D<float> density SRV
Camera params: view-proj or ray dir generation in CS, right-handed, Y-up
Directional light: world-space dir, intensity, color; self-shadow by marching toward light
Controls: densityScale, absorption, maxSteps, stepSize, lightDir, lightColor (Phase 1 via keys)
Temporal hooks: optional history buffer (to be activated in VOL_0004)
Barriers: density SRV, HDR UAV; insert UAV barrier, then HDR UAV→SRV for composite
steps: Inputs: bind density SRV (t#), HDR UAV (u#), camera constants, volume params constants
Ray gen: per-pixel eye ray; intersect a fixed AABB ([-bounds, +bounds])
Integrate: accumulate emission/absorption along the ray; for shadowing, do short ray to light per step or every N steps
Write: HDR color; optional tonemap later in composite PS
CMake: add compile for raymarch.dxil; copy on build
Validation: add heartbeat log every ~60 frames with average steps and occupancy
acceptance_criteria: Distinct volumetric appearance with a moving light or camera
No device removal; PIX shows raymarch dispatch plus HDR composite
Runtime controls adjust look in real time; parameters logged on change
